To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we derived new bounds for the error induced by POD model reduction using snapshots from the solutions or the solutions and their derivatives.

the POD method that uses snapshots from the solution only is not as accurate as the method that uses snapshots of both the solution and time derivative, and that the POD method using snapshots of both the solutions and time derivatives is more accurate for the FitzHugh-Naguumo system.
the error bounds provide insights and justification of the use of time derivative snapshots in proper orthogonal decomposition model reductions for dynamical systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and development of proper orthogonal decomposition methods and error bounds for reduced order modeling.

the development of new error bounds for the approximation error in proper orthogonal decomposition methods and the investigation of the relation between the error bounds and the numerically observed errors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the error bounds are a valuable tool in POD model reduction and the use of time derivative snapshots in the POD model reduction method is a good idea.
the error bounds derived for the two POD model reduction methods are not tight but do provide insights and justification to use time derivative snapshots in model reduction.
, in general, the use of time derivatives in the POD method does not necessarily lead to a more accurate approximation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the semidiscretization of the FitzHugh-Naguno system, using time derivative snapshots is better than using only the solution snapshots.
, if we have the time derivative information of the solution at hand, we can improve the accuracy of the POD model by using both the solution and its derivative as the basis.
, for the semidiscretizations of PDEs, POD methods based on snapshots of the solutions and their derivatives are more effective than POD methods based on solution snapshots only.
The main takeaway from our work is that
using snapshots of the solution and the first time derivative can improve the quality of reduced models.
, for systems where the first neglected singular values are small, using time derivative snapshots is a viable option to improve the accuracy of the reduced model.
, when using POD to reduce the size of a dynamical system, it is beneficial to collect snapshots of the solutions as well as the time derivatives of the solution.
